meaning: Carcharhinus, from Greek karcharias “a kind of shark” (from karcharos “saw-like, jagged”, for its teeth) + rhinus, an ancient word for sharks; acronotus, from Greek akron “summit, top” + notos “back”, the allusion not explained, perhaps referring to a “raised” back at the first dorsal fin
description: A slender, greenish-grey shark with a long rounded snout, large eyes and a small first dorsal fin. Young sharks have a dark blotch at the tip of the snout, and the second dorsal fin and upper tail lobe have dark tips. It is a fast, schooling shark of warm western Atlantic shelf waters, and groups often return to the same areas year after year.
eats: Small bony fish such as pinfish, croakers and porgies, also octopus and other cephalopods
